title: SOVITECH extraction contract
description: The one source of the JSON exchanged between the Python extractor (services/extractor) and the API (apps/api): the extraction request, the extraction output per file, and the strict shape of Evidence.locator that the evidence verifier reads. The zod schemas (packages/extraction-contract/src/generated/zod.ts) and the Python dataclasses (services/extractor/src/sovitech_extractor/contract/_generated.py, with a copy of this file as schema.json) are generated from it; edit this file and run the generator. Every object is closed: a key this file does not name is refused. No engineering value travels as a JSON number: numbers read from a document stay text (PDF text, XLSX cached values, STEP literal tokens) for the rule 8 parser in packages/registry. JSON numbers are only page numbers, character offsets, STEP instance ids, model-check counts and PDF coordinates. See packages/extraction-contract/README.md.

Uuid.description: A lower-case UUID, as the app generates ids (UUIDv7 in app code).

ContentHash.description: SHA-256 of a file's bytes, in the store's form: 'sha256:' and 64 lower-case hex digits.

Code.description: A machine code (a reason, a detector or a validator rule), never document text.

VersionText.description: A version as its tool writes it.

ToolVersion.description: A tool or library and its version.

DatasetRef.description: A dataset and its version (a mapping table, the glossary, the asset taxonomy). Naming one approves nothing: approval is read from stored approval records (G1-12).

Format.description: The file format, set by code from the file content (ifc-input 6.2.2 lists the same formats, with images split by type so that the G12-1 line can name them).

Coordinate.description: A PDF coordinate in points, in the page space PDFium reports.

Box.description: [left, bottom, right, top] in the PDF page space PDFium reports (points, y upwards). Left is never past right, and bottom never above top.

SheetName.description: An XLSX sheet name as written: 1 to 31 characters, none of the characters Excel refuses in a sheet name.

CellRef.description: An A1 cell reference, upper case, no $ signs.

RangeRef.description: An A1 range, for merged cells.

AnchorId.description: The id of one text block, unique in one extraction output. The AI may cite it; the API turns it into a page and a bbox for Evidence.locator.

GlobalId.description: An IFC GlobalId: 22 characters of the IFC base-64 alphabet. Never an identity across models (ifc-identity gate).

StepId.description: A STEP instance id (#n) in the file with the output's content hash.

IfcSchemaId.description: The schema the file header declares, as written: IFC2X3, IFC4, IFC4X3_ADD2 and so on.

IfcClassName.description: An IFC entity class as IfcOpenShell names it (IfcPump, IfcBuildingElementProxy).

IfcTypeName.description: The defined type of a typed STEP literal as the STEP file writes it (IFCPOWERMEASURE, IFCLABEL).

FactId.description: The id of one IFC fact, unique in one extraction output.

ProposalId.description: The id of one IFC candidate proposal, unique in one extraction output.

FieldKey.description: A field registry key (packages/registry), such as building.grossFloorArea.

IfcGateId.description: A gate an IFC candidate proposal waits for (prompt 3 section 5.4; packages/registry/gates/). Every one is a registry gate id.

DerivativeKind.description: A viewing derivative: converted geometry (Fragments, GLB), a storey plan as SVG with no text, a thumbnail, a PDF page image.

ExtractionRequest.description: What the API asks of the extractor for one stored file (one job; ADR 0020: job payloads carry ids, and the worker mounts the file read-only at a fixed path).

ifcValues.description: Emit IFC facts and candidate proposals. The API sets it from readGate('ifc-values'): false while the gate is closed, so no mapping table is consulted (PRD R-027, 'Until decided').

datasets.description: Datasets mounted for the IFC candidate proposals (mapping tables, glossary, taxonomy). Empty unless ifcValues is true.

Limits.description: Work limits for one job; the sandbox also kills the container on its wall clock (ADR 0018). Reaching a limit is coverage, never silence (rule 12).

Job.description: The file the job read: its project, its document record and the content hash of the bytes it read.

ExtractionOutput.description: Everything the extractor read from one file. It never writes the database and proposes nothing from PDF or XLSX content: those candidates come from the AI and the verifier (prompt 3 section 6).

Producer.description: The extractor build that wrote the output, with the libraries that read the file.

AnalysisStatus.description: The file's analysis status in the terms of the 2.8 status lines, as code recorded it (F-INGEST-05). An IFC file is always stored_only with 'IFC model' under guardrails v1.6: its values are not read, so it never counts as analysed coverage (G12-5). What the extractor could process in a model is ifcModel.processing, for the engineer.

AnalysedStatus.description: Every page or sheet was read.

PartlyAnalysedStatus.description: Some of the file was read and some was not (rule 12, 'Partial processing is shown with its coverage'; 2.3 'partly_analysed'). For a PDF, the pages read of its pages: 'Partly analysed (<read> of <total> pages)' (2.8; G12-3). For an XLSX workbook, the sheets read of its sheets; the owner-facing line for sheets waits for the approver (build log, P-2-XLSX-SHEETS), so the status is stored, not shown as new wording. Both numbers are recorded by code and bound on screen to the document's coverage.

StoredOnlyStatus.description: 'Not analysed: <formatWord> stored, not analysed' (2.8; G12-1). The word fills the slot the way G12-1 names RVT; the words other than 'RVT model' are substitutions listed for the approver as a wording clarification (prompt 3 section 5.3).

AnalysisFailedStatus.description: 'Analysis failed' (2.8). The reason is a code for the engineer and the logs; it is never shown as its own status wording.

Coverage.description: What code read and what it could not read, and why (rule 12; F-INGEST-05). A page, sheet or model part listed as not read supports no 'Not found in the analysed documents' statement (G12-4).

PageCoverage.description: Pages read and not read. Together they cover pages 1 to total, each page once.

UnreadPageRange.description: Pages not read. With no OCR (prompt 3 section 5.2), a page with no text layer is not read (G12-3 is built with such pages).

SheetCoverage.description: One sheet of the workbook, read or not, with the reason when not.

IfcCoverage.description: For the engineer's view only (R-023): the entity classes read, and what could not be read. It is not an owner-facing coverage line and never counts the model as searched (G12-5).

IfcUnread.description: A part of the model that could not be read, with a code for why. Codes, GlobalIds and STEP ids only, never model text (prompt 3 section 8).

PdfContent.description: The native text layer of each page read (pypdfium2; F-EXTRACT-01). No OCR.

PdfPage.description: One page read: its media box, its rotation and its text blocks in reading order.

TextBlock.description: A run of text as the page's text layer holds it, raw: the extractor never reads a number out of it. A block with hidden reasons is reported as a hidden_text finding and gives no values (rule 14): it is never part of the text evidence is checked against.

charBoxes.description: Character boxes: each covers the code points start (inclusive) to end (exclusive) of text. Characters the text layer does not place (inserted spaces, line breaks) have none.

layer.description: The optional-content group (layer) name as written, when the block is on one.

PdfHiddenReason.description: Why a text block counts as hidden text (rule 14: white or tiny text, content outside the page, hidden layers).

XlsxContent.description: Each sheet of the workbook with its cells (openpyxl; F-EXTRACT-01).

XlsxCell.description: One cell with a cached value. raw is the cached value exactly as the file stores it (the text of a number cell as written in the sheet XML, the string of a string cell), never a number the extractor computed or reformatted; numberFormat is the format code as written.

formula.description: The formula as written, when the cell has one. Data, never evaluated.

XlsxHiddenReason.description: Why a cell counts as hidden text (rule 14).

IfcModelRecord.description: The engineer-only record of a stored model (R-023, F-IFC-01, F-IFC-09): the header as written, the classes present, what the extractor could process, the schema check and the IDS results. Not a DocumentRecord field (DocumentRecord.model is ifc-input 6.2.2, behind ifc-values), never a value, never evidence, never an owner-facing line, count or task. Readable while ifc-values is closed.

authoringTool.description: The originating system from the file header, as written. Data (rule 14), never logged (rule 13).

SchemaCheck.description: Whether ifcopenshell.validate ran and whether it found problems. The problems themselves are schema_error findings with codes.

IdsRef.description: An IDS file by id, version and hash. The SOVITECH IDS stays 'draft' until the approver accepts it (ifc-input 5.5).

IdsResults.description: IDS results as spec ids, counts and failing GlobalIds, never report text (prompt 3 section 8). Engineer's view only; never a candidate, a question, an open item or a coverage line (ifc-values, while closed).

IfcValues.description: SEALED. IFC facts and the table-driven IFC candidate proposals. The API reads them only through openIfcValues() with a gate source, and only while ifc-values is open; each proposal also waits for its own gates. Under guardrails v1.6 Evidence.locator has no IFC field, so nothing here becomes a candidate while ifc-values is closed (ifc-input 6.2.1; G1-13). The IFC locator lives here and nowhere else: it is never written into page, sheet, cell or bbox (prompt 3 section 8).

IfcFact.description: One value read from the model, with its IFC locator and the verbatim STEP text of the lines that hold it (ifc-input 4.1 item 3). The excerpt keeps STEP string escapes as written (\X2\...\X0\).

IfcLocator.description: The IFC locator of ifc-input 6.2.1 (a proposal): the file by content hash, its declared schema, the element's GlobalId, the STEP instance ids of the quoted lines, and the path to the value.

IfcPath.description: Where the value sits, from the element: an attribute, a property of a property set, a quantity of a quantity set (each on the occurrence or through its type object), or a relation to another element.

StepValue.description: A typed STEP literal, kept as its token. A real or an integer stays text here; the API reads it, never the extractor (prompt 3 section 6).

StepScalar.description: A STEP literal that is not a list, for the items of a list.

StepString.description: token is the STEP string as written, quotes and escapes included; text is the decoded string (the Candidate's original.text).

StepReference.description: A reference to another instance (#n) of the same file.

StepUnset.description: $: the attribute is not set. Unknown, never zero (rule 1).

StepDerived.description: *: the value is derived by the schema, not written in the file.

DeclaredUnit.description: The unit the file declares for a value, as written: from the project's unit assignment or from the value's own Unit (ifc-input 4.1 item 4). Mapping it to a registry unit, with the dimension check, is the API's (2.7); an unmapped unit gives no quantity candidate.

IfcCandidateProposal.description: A table-driven candidate proposal from the model (ifc-input 4.1 item 2). A proposal, never a candidate: the API verifies it and decides its source (rule 1; 2.1). It carries no parsed number: a quantity comes from its fact's STEP token through the API.

sourceClaim.description: The source the extractor claims. Code decides the source (2.1): 'calculated' only with the geometry mechanism (ifc-input 6.2.7, behind ifc-geometry).

datasets.description: The mapping tables and other datasets that shaped the proposal, with their versions (ifc-input 6.2.10).

confidence.description: For ai_inference only; code caps it again against the evidence (rule 3).

ProposalSubject.description: The subject kind and the model element the proposal is about. Resolving it to a subject is the API's, under ifc-identity (GlobalId is not an identity across models).

IfcProposalMechanism.description: How the extractor made the proposal. x-mechanism-rules gives the gates each mechanism waits for at least, and whether it needs a dataset.

FactProposalValue.description: The value is one of the evidence facts' value, read by the API (a STEP token through the rule 8 parser or the typed literal reader).

ChoiceProposalValue.description: An enum key from a mapping table (an asset type, a level type, a system).

Finding.description: An item for the engineer (rule 14; F-EXTRACT-10, F-IFC-01, F-IFC-02). A code and a location, never document text. A finding creates no candidate, badge, verification or field state. Readable while ifc-values is closed (G14-3).

FindingLocator.description: Where a finding is. An IFC finding names GlobalIds and STEP ids for the engineer; this is not Evidence.locator.

FileFindingLocator.description: The file as a whole (its header or metadata).

Derivative.description: A viewing file derived from the document, stored under <projectId>/<contentHash>/derived/ and keyed by project id plus content hash (G13-4): never shared between projects, served only after the project access check, removed by the erasure job with its document (ifc-input 6.2.16, a stricter build choice). Never cited as evidence (prompt 3 section 8).

EvidenceLocator.description: The strict runtime shape of guardrails 2.4 Evidence.locator that the evidence verifier reads (rule 1, 'The locator exists'; G1-13). A PDF locator (page, with an optional bbox) or an XLSX locator (sheet, with an optional cell). Any other key is refused: there is no IFC field (no GlobalId, STEP id or path) until the approver accepts ifc-input 6.2.1. x-ifc-locator-keys lists the keys that would carry one; both parsers refuse them with the code ifc_field, for the verifier's log (G1-13).
